questions.scenario: Your younger sibling is throwing a massive tantrum at the supermarket because your mom won't buy them a Kinder Joy. What do you do?

options.A: I hold their hand and give them a physical task like carrying a small basket to distract their motor skills.
options.B: I observe the trigger and realize they only cry near the candy aisle when they missed their afternoon nap.
options.C: I make a funny face, grab a colorful packet, and make up an entertaining, animated story to change their mood.
options.D: I tell my parents to finish the billing while I step in to firmly negotiate a deal with my sibling.

questions.scenario: Your friend broke their writing hand right before the pre-board exams. How do you help?

options.A: I teach them some hand-stretching exercises to reduce the pain and help them practice writing with their left hand.
options.B: I create a highly structured, logical timetable to ensure they finish studying the syllabus orally without wasting time.
options.C: I teach them to use voice notes and draw colorful mind maps so they can memorize points without writing paragraphs.
options.D: I go straight to the class teacher and principal to officially arrange a scribe (writer) for their board exams.

questions.scenario: Your younger cousin is struggling to learn the English alphabet and keeps forgetting the letters.

options.A: I physically guide their fingers to trace the letters in a plate of atta (flour) or sand so they feel the shapes.
options.B: I analyze their mistakes and realize they only get confused between similar mirror shapes like 'b' and 'd'.
options.C: I sing a funny Hindi rhyming song, assigning a silly animal to every letter to make it creatively memorable.
options.D: I suggest a highly-rated local tuition teacher to their parents and organize a fixed study schedule for them.

questions.scenario: A shy new student joins your class mid-term and is sitting completely alone during recess.

options.A: I go sit next to them, share my tiffin, and physically take them on a walking tour of the entire school campus.
options.B: I silently observe who they look at during class to figure out exactly which friend group they would fit into best.
options.C: I notice they are doodling in their rough notebook and start drawing with them to break the ice without words.
options.D: I ask the class monitor to formally introduce them to everyone so they instantly feel integrated into the system.

questions.scenario: Your residential society is organizing a grand Diwali mela. What is your main job?

options.A: I take charge of the heavy lifting—setting up the game stalls, hanging the fairy lights, and moving the chairs.
options.B: I make a master spreadsheet tracking exactly who is bringing what so there are zero duplicate food stalls.
options.C: I design a massive, vibrant rangoli for the entrance and curate the perfect festive Bollywood playlist.
options.D: I collect the 'chanda' (donation) from all flats, manage the budget, and coordinate with the chief guest.

questions.scenario: A stray dog in your gully is slightly injured and looks very scared.

options.A: I slowly approach it, pet it gently to calm its nerves, and carefully wrap a clean cloth around its injured paw.
options.B: I observe its body language from a distance to logically predict if it is aggressive before deciding what to do.
options.C: I speak to it in a soothing, high-pitched 'baby voice' and offer a Parle-G biscuit to gently win its trust.
options.D: I instantly call the local animal NGO helpline and organize my neighbors to keep the dog safe until help arrives.

questions.scenario: Your best friend gets extremely anxious and sweaty right before the Chemistry practical viva.

options.A: I show them deep breathing exercises and make them stretch their shoulders to physically release the built-up tension.
options.B: I ask them which topic scares them and logically explain why the examiner statistically probably won't ask that.
options.C: I tell them to vividly imagine the strict examiner wearing a funny clown suit to make the situation less terrifying.
options.D: I wait outside the lab, give them a firm pep talk, and ask the previous batch exactly what questions were asked.

questions.scenario: You have been given the ultimate responsibility of teaching your grandparents how to use WhatsApp.

options.A: I physically hold their hands to show them exactly how hard to tap, swipe, and scroll on the glass screen.
options.B: I figure out exactly which buttons confuse them the most and write down a clear, logical step-by-step instruction list.
options.C: I change their wallpaper to a family photo and teach them how to use tons of emojis to make chatting fun and expressive.
options.D: I assign turns to my younger siblings so the 'teaching load' is managed efficiently across everyone in the house.

questions.scenario: You have an old, rusty bicycle at home that nobody uses. What's your plan for it?

options.A: I grab a wrench, take it apart, oil the rusty chain, and fix the pedals so someone can actually ride it again.
options.B: I research the broken parts to calculate if repairing it is mathematically cheaper than just buying a new one.
options.C: I paint the frame neon green and turn the front basket into a quirky, creative flower pot for the balcony.
options.D: I sell the metal for scrap to the local raddi-wala and manage the cash to buy a football for the street kids.

questions.scenario: The grumpy society uncle is complaining about you and your friends playing cricket in the parking lot.

options.A: I quickly move our game to the nearby park and physically mark out the new boundary lines with our slippers.
options.B: I observe the uncle's daily routine and figure out the exact time he takes his afternoon nap so we can play then.
options.C: I invent a new version of 'silent cricket' using a soft sponge ball and rolled-up newspaper bats to avoid noise.
options.D: I call a formal meeting with the society secretary to designate a specific 'play zone' timing for all the kids.

Occupational_Therapist.title: Occupational / Physical Therapist
Occupational_Therapist.primary_match_text: The Hands-On Healer! You love being active and physically helping people. You are practical, patient, and believe in taking action.
Occupational_Therapist.day_in_the_life: Helping kids with special needs improve their physical movements. You use gym balls, swings, and practical tasks (like tying shoelaces) to help them build strength and coordinate their bodies.
Occupational_Therapist.alternative_match_text: Physiotherapist, Sports Rehabilitation Coach, Ergonomics Expert
Occupational_Therapist.roadmap: 11th/12th (Science - PCB) -> Bachelor of Occupational Therapy (BOT) or Physiotherapy (BPT) -> Register with Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI) -> Master's (MOT/MPT) in Pediatrics.

Behavioral_Analyst.title: Behavioral Analyst
Behavioral_Analyst.primary_match_text: The Pattern Decoder! You are observant, logical, and notice the tiny details others miss. You like figuring out the 'why' behind how people act.
Behavioral_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Observing children to understand their behavior patterns. You figure out what triggers a meltdown and create structured, step-by-step plans to help them learn positive social behaviors.
Behavioral_Analyst.roadmap: 11th/12th (Arts or Science with Psychology) -> B.A/B.Sc in Psychology -> Master's in Clinical or Applied Psychology -> Certification in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA).

Art_Play_Therapist.title: Art / Play Therapist
Art_Play_Therapist.primary_match_text: The Creative Empath! You are highly expressive and use creativity—like colors, music, and games—to solve emotional problems and connect with others.
Art_Play_Therapist.day_in_the_life: Using drawing, music, clay, and toys to help children who struggle to express themselves with words. You create a safe space for them to process feelings and communicate through play.
Art_Play_Therapist.alternative_match_text: Child Psychologist, Creative Arts Teacher, Expressive Arts Counselor
Art_Play_Therapist.roadmap: 11th/12th (Arts/Humanities) -> B.A in Psychology, Sociology, or Fine Arts -> Master's in Psychology -> PG Diploma or Certification in Art Therapy or Play Therapy.

Center_Director.title: Special Ed Center Director
Center_Director.primary_match_text: The Impact Leader! You are a natural manager who handles crises, organizes systems, and looks at the big picture to create massive change.
Center_Director.day_in_the_life: Running an entire inclusive school or NGO. You meet with concerned parents, manage the center's budget, hire top therapists, and talk to donors to secure funding for the children.
Center_Director.alternative_match_text: NGO Founder, School Principal, Social Entrepreneur
Center_Director.roadmap: 11th/12th (Any Stream) -> B.Ed in Special Education, BSW, or BBA -> Master of Social Work (MSW), M.Ed, or an MBA in NGO/Education Management.
